strongest_angle: The discovery of a 1963 photographic archive by Elizabeth Tyler offers a rare, intimate look at Coventry's post-war bomb sites, preserved for six decades before being rediscovered in Sweden.

key_facts.fact: In 1963, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler captured images of bomb sites and abandoned buildings in Coventry using a second-hand camera.
The photographic archive was moved across four different countries over the course of six decades before being rediscovered in an attic.
Elizabeth Tyler, now 80 years old, was a student at the Coventry College of Art when she took the original photographs.
The collection of black and white photographs remained stored in a box in an attic in Borstahusen, Sweden, for more than 60 years.
